I will keep all 5.0 mu in cotton, because my land is small, I know this crop well after 40 years, and at my age I value a stable, familiar system over changing to something new. Since I have well irrigation, I will manage for steady production rather than gambling on rain. I will use improved seed, not traditional seed, because I want more uniform emergence and better yield without the extra cost and management pressure that can come with more intensive choices. I will plough before planting, because I prefer a clean seedbed and good root development at the start of the season. For fertilizer, I will apply a moderate program with nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium together so the crop has balanced growth. I will irrigate a few key times during establishment, flowering, and boll setting, because that is where water matters most for cotton on my farm. I will spray pesticides only as much as needed to protect the crop through the main pest periods, but I will not run a very high-input program on just 5 mu. With this approach, I am aiming for a solid, realistic yield rather than the highest possible yield.
